title: Recording with Tiny Parham, Dutrey and Ory

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: That's a good record. Tell me some more about Tiny Parham. About how many records did you do with him?
Oh, my goodness, I don't have any idea. I did a lot of them, come to find out.
What label?
Victor. But we was recording quite a bit. Because he used to write the tunes. And about this time, used to do six sides. Sometimes eight sides. Did you ever hear of 'Head-Hunter's Dream'?
No.
That was one of the records we made.
"A Head-Hunter's Dream"?
Uh-huh.
Didn't Junie Cobb play some with him?
I can't remember. I believe so.
He's another sort of mystery man in jazz history.
Yeah.
I'm never quite sure whether he plays trumpet or tuba.
Saxophone.
Saxophone?
Yeah. He was way ahead of me.
Didn't he have a brother, also, who played?
Yeah. I can't think of his brother's name. I think his brother played trumpet.
Maybe that's who I'm thinking of.
Yeah, had a brother played trumpet.
I remember one record, great name for a band, "Junie Cobb and his Ears of Corn."
Yeah.
Well, how often would you record with Tiny Parham? You said you recorded a lot. Once a month? Couple times a month?
Several times a month, I'd say.
And the records would come out quickly in those days.
Yeah, they would come out real quick.
Well, were they played a lot on jukeboxes? I mean, what was the -- you know, the people he was aiming for?
I don't know.
Well, did he work gigs around town?
Yeah, worked steady with him at the ______, for a while, 35th and State.
Yeah? When was that?
That was first, it had to be before Earl Hines.

Yeah, must have been. A little before '29, before '30, because '29 I was in the Metropolitan Theater. I went in the Metropolitan Theater in '28. This must have been around the same time I recorded with Jelly Roll, right
around '27. Who were some of the guys that were on those recording dates with Tiny?
Omer Simeon, Shirley Clay, and -- I can't think who -- oh, Preston Jackson made some.
Were you playing tuba or string bass?

Tuba. I hadn't started on string bass yet. Tiny played piano. I'm trying to remember who played drums on that. Preston Jackson, I think, may have been on trombone. I don't remember whether Dutrey or Kid Ory was in on them records or not. Because they were doing a lot of recording with the same bands.
Did you play some with Orey?
Yeah. Played with Dutrey.
Recording or gigs?
Recording.
What was your impression of the New Orleans musicians?
Well, they was all the same to me. Yeah, we got along fine. Just like Chicago musicians. I never had any trouble with them.
Certainly recorded with a lot of fine people, played with a lot of fine people.
Uh-huh.
